data.raw_text:
A man faked his own death in a canoe accident, collected £250,000 in life insurance and hid next door to his own house for years.

– In March 2002 John Darwin paddled his canoe into the North Sea off the English coast and vanished.

– Police launched a massive search. They found fragments of a red kayak. No body. A death certificate was issued.

– Anne collected £250,000 in life insurance and pension payouts and grieved publicly.

– John had not gone far. He was living in the bedsit next door to their family home the entire time, hidden behind a door connecting the two properties.

– Their two sons believed their father was dead for years. Anne looked them in the eye and said nothing.

– Eventually a hidden bedsit was not enough. They wanted a real life.

– They flew to Panama, looked at property and took photos smiling with a local real estate agent.

– In December 2007 John walked into a London police station and claimed he had amnesia. Said he remembered nothing from the last five years.

– Police were taking it seriously.

– Then a woman who had read the news story simply typed "John Anne Panama" into Google Images.

– The first result was a photo from a website called https://t.co/HYlRk7UrsN. John and Anne standing together grinning beside a Panamanian property agent. Timestamp: July 4 2006.

– She emailed it anonymously to the Daily Mirror and Cleveland Police the same day.

– The Daily Mirror ran it on the front page under the headline: "CANOE'S THIS IN PANAMA?"

– Anne's response when confronted with the photo: "Yes that's him. My sons will never forgive me."

– John got 6 years and 3 months. Anne got 6 years and 6 months.

– John now lives in the Philippines with a wife 33 years younger than him.

They faked a death, hid next door to their own house, collected £250,000, and moved to Panama. A random woman with a Google search found them in seconds. Their sons found out their father was alive from a newspaper front page.

data.raw_text:
Most people only think of @MeteoraAG as the protocol for LPing.

But over the past year, the ecosystem has grown into something way bigger.

Meteora isn't just about liquidity pools, but it's quickly becoming a key piece of @solana DeFi.

Here's the full breakdown:

1. @MeteoraAG: The central hub

The main account where you hear about all the major product releases and announcements from the team.

Just last week, the team shipped Limit Orders and Quote Token Fees. If you want more alpha, this is the channel.

2. @met_lparmy: The community backbone

Over 20,000 retail market makers pushing LPing into every corner of the world. These are the power users of Meteora, giving out education for FREE and pushing each other to grow every single day. Led by @Heavymetalcook6, @AlekssRG and @memecoinassasin.

The LP Army also has a global presence with regional units across France, Spain, Indonesia, Nigeria, Malaysia, Philippines and many more, all coordinated, all shipping with the goal of pushing Meteora on every corner of the world.

3. @MeteoraEco: The capital markets layer.

IRL events, hackathons, spaces, you name it. Meteora Ecosystem is where all the builders and founders come together to push the boundaries of capital markets together, with strong presence in recent IRL activations like MtnDAO and Solana Skyline. Led by @vesper792.

4. @MeteoraInside: The investor relations arm. 

Full transparent on-chain data at https://t.co/b74ftqafrI, and public metrics that you can see. Meteora is one of the few protocols to score a perfect 40/40 on the Blockworks Token Transparency Filing. Led by @pranave.

5. @BedrockFndn: the venture arm for tokenized startups. 

@0xSoju said it best: there are going to be millions of founders and startups, and every one of them will need funding. 

Bedrock recently completed its first raise.

Bedrock is the bridge connecting crypto capital to the next wave of founders.

Meteora started off as the liquidity layer, but now is expanding into the full infrastructure for all things capital markets on Solana, layer by layer.

Meteora is not just a DEX, but an ecosystem.

If you're not bullish on Meteora yet, you need to start paying more attention.
